problem.title: Sequential Readmission Severity Update via DO Block
problem.prompt: A hospital tracks patient admissions in the `patient_admissions` table. When a patient is readmitted within 30 days of discharge, the severity level needs to be escalated based on specific rules. Write a DO block that processes admissions in chronological order (by admission_date, then admission_id) and applies these rules sequentially: (1) If a patient was discharged and readmitted within 30 days, increase their new admission's severity_score by 10. (2) After applying rule 1, if the resulting severity_score exceeds 75, set the high_risk flag to TRUE. (3) After applying rules 1 and 2, if high_risk is TRUE and the patient is over 65 years old, increase severity_score by an additional 5. Process each admission using the values as they exist after prior rules have been applied. After the DO block, include a SELECT statement that returns all columns from patient_admissions ordered by admission_id.
problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE patient_admissions (admission_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, patient_id INTEGER NOT NULL, patient_age INTEGER NOT NULL, admission_date DATE NOT NULL, discharge_date DATE, severity_score INTEGER NOT NULL, high_risk BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE);

composite_moves: trailing SELECT to display mutated state

hints: You need to process admissions one by one in chronological order, checking if each admission is a readmission within 30 days of a prior discharge for the same patient.

Use a CURSOR or FOR loop to iterate through admissions ordered by admission_date and admission_id. For each admission, look for the most recent prior discharge for that patient and check the day difference.

Apply the three rules in sequence for each admission: first add 10 if readmitted within 30 days, then check if severity_score > 75 to set high_risk, then add 5 more if high_risk is TRUE and patient_age > 65. Use the updated values at each step.

_meta.scenario: a hospital system tracking patient admissions, discharges, and readmissions
